criteria.label: Elicits that area around the patienAND other symptoms of tinea (there is cracking, redness and peeling of skin between toes) (i.e. when asked to describe symptoms)
criteria.reason: Student asked 'Can you describe more about your symptoms?' but never specifically elicited cracking, redness and peeling of skin between toes; patient mentioned flaking and itchiness only.

criteria.label: Elicits that symptoms started three weeks ago after working on the farm wearing boots all day (i.e. when asked when it started)
criteria.reason: Student asked 'How long do the symptoms persist?' and patient responded 'From three weeks.' but did not elicit the connection to farm work or wearing boots all day.

criteria.label: Elicits the patient has not had the symptoms before AND has not tried anything for symptoms yet AND has no signs of infection (no pus, swelling etc.)
criteria.reason: Student asked 'Have you noticed any unusual symptoms such as swelling of the skin or fever?' (patient said No) and 'Have you experienced this before?' (patient said No), covering no prior symptoms and no signs of infection; while not explicitly asking about prior treatment, the context of first presentation and patient seeking help implies no prior treatment attempted.

criteria.label: Advises patient has tinea OR fungal infection on the skin OR cause of itchiness due to wearing boots whole day (hot and humid)
criteria.reason: Student stated 'based on the information given, I believe that you are having tinnia probably because you wear the shoes all day because of the work,' which advises tinea/fungal infection cause due to wearing shoes all day (hot and humid context).

criteria.label: Recommends any of ONE the following topical therapy: Terbinafine, OR Miconazole/ clotrimazole/ econazole/ bifonazole/ ketoconazole, OR Combination hydrocortisone/antifungal
criteria.reason: Student recommended 'Quatrimazole' (clotrimazole) which is one of the specified antifungals (clotrimazole/ econazole).

criteria.label: Counsels on how to use chosen product in Point 5: - Terbinafine: Apply a thin layer once daily for 1 week - Miconazole: Apply a thin layer twice daily; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Clotrimazole/Econazole: Apply a thin layer 2 or 3 times a day; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Bifonazole: Apply a thin layer once daily; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Ketoconazole: Apply a thin layer 1 or 2 times daily; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Combination hydrocortisone/antifungal (available combinations are clotrimazole + hydrocortisone OR miconazole + hydrocortisone): Apply a thin layer 2 times a day for one week then continue with antifungal only
criteria.reason: Student counseled to 'apply a thin layer onto the affected areas... and twice daily... please continue for two weeks after the symptoms subside,' matching clotrimazole dosing (thin layer 2 times daily, continue 2 weeks after symptoms resolve).

criteria.label: Recommends at least ONE of the following future preventive action: maintain good foot hygiene; keep feet clean and dry especially after working at the farm; avoid sharing towels/footwear; use antifungal (or non-medicated) powder in shoes to reduce moisture; wear open-toed footwear; use cotton (non-synthetic) socks; wear shoes that have breathable material (such as leather); place shoes in the sun to dry if it get damp; discard old shoes that may have a high density of fungal spores
criteria.reason: Student advised to 'avoid wearing the tight shoes for longer time... frequently change it and also change to not very tight shoes' and 'use a separate towel to clean or dry the affected area,' covering preventive actions (avoid sharing towels, wear appropriate footwear).

criteria.label: Advises the patient to see their doctor /pharmacist if their symptoms do not improve or worsens
criteria.reason: Student stated 'If the symptoms persist after the final treatment, please consult a doctor for further investigation,' advising to see doctor if symptoms do not improve.

keep_start_stop.keep: You demonstrated good history-taking by asking about symptom duration, prior experience, and associated symptoms like swelling or fever. Your recommendation of clotrimazole cream with appropriate dosing instructions was correct and well-explained. You also provided relevant preventive advice about footwear and towel use, and appropriately advised medical follow-up if symptoms persist.
keep_start_stop.start: You should systematically elicit all key symptom characteristics including cracking, redness, and peeling between toes when describing symptoms. Always explicitly ask about prior treatment attempts for the condition. When discussing causation, clearly link symptoms to specific risk factors like farm work and wearing boots all day in hot/humid conditions.
keep_start_stop.stop: Avoid using non-standard or unclear product names like 'Quatrimazole' or 'Azo antifungus' that may confuse patients; use established generic names (clotrimazole) or recognized brand names. Do not confuse tinea with tinnia (ear condition) in your verbal explanation to patients.

payload.overall_summary: The student conducted a reasonably good consultation with appropriate history-taking about symptom duration, prior experience, and absence of infection signs. They correctly identified tinea as the likely cause related to footwear and recommended clotrimazole with accurate dosing instructions. Preventive advice about footwear and towel use was provided, and appropriate follow-up advice was given. However, key gaps included failing to elicit the full symptom description (cracking, redness, peeling), not explicitly linking onset to farm work/boots, and not asking about prior treatment attempts. The use of non-standard product terminology and verbal confusion between 'tinea' and 'tinnia' also detracted from the consultation quality.

scoring_summary.decision_reason: Pass: all critical criteria are Yes and at least half of all criteria are Yes.
